title: TARP capital injection on bank risk-taking

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
The causal method appropriate for this analysis is Difference-in-Differences (DID). This method is suitable because it allows us to compare changes in outcomes over time between a treatment group (TARP recipient banks) and a control group (non-recipient banks). The key assumption for DID is the parallel trends assumption, which implies that in the absence of treatment, the difference in outcomes between the treated and control groups would have remained constant over time. We will visually inspect the pre-treatment trends to assess the plausibility of this assumption.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the dataset
file_path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s04_data.csv"
data <- read_csv(file_path)

# Convert to factor variables as needed
data <- data %>%
  mutate(unit_id = as.factor(unit_id),
         period = as.factor(period))

# Run the Difference-in-Differences regression
did_model <- lm(y ~ treated * post, data = data)

# Summary with robust standard errors
coeftest(did_model, vcov = vcovHC(did_model, type = "HC1"))

# Basic robustness check: Inspect pre-treatment trends
pre_trend_check <- data %>%
  filter(post == 0) %>%
  group_by(period, treated) %>%
  summarise(mean_y = mean(y)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = period, y = mean_y, color = factor(treated))) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Pre-treatment Trends", x = "Period", y = "Mean Non-performing Loan Ratio", color = "Treated") +
  theme_minimal()

print(pre_trend_check)

# Extract and print the DID effect
did_effect <- summary(did_model)$coefficients["treated:post", "Estimate"]
cat("The estimated DID effect of TARP on risk-taking is:", did_effect, "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
We expect the sign of the DID coefficient to be positive, indicating that TARP capital injections increased risk-taking among recipient banks. The magnitude will depend on the specific effects of TARP funding on bank behavior, but we anticipate a modest increase in the non-performing loan ratio given that capital injections could encourage riskier lending practices due to a safety net effect. However, the exact magnitude needs to be determined through empirical analysis.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=TARP recipients, control=non-recipients; parallel pre-trends required
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: TARP banks show higher NPL ratios post-injection, consistent with moral hazard
_ground_truth.main_effect: 20bp increase in NPL ratio for TARP banks
